ITEM 2. - DETAILS OF ACQUISITION

 

2.1 Nature of Business Acquired

 

On August 28, 2026, the Company completed its previously announced acquisition (the “Acquisition”) of all of the issued and outstanding shares of GeoPura Limited (“GeoPura”) by the Company’s wholly-owned subsidiary (the “Buyer”) pursuant to a share purchase agreement dated June 23, 2026 (the “Purchase Agreement”) entered into between, among others, the Company, the Buyer and those persons whose names and addresses are set out in Schedule 1 thereto (the “Sellers”).

 

GeoPura, founded in 2019 and headquartered in Newcastle, United Kingdom, is a provider of zero-emission, hydrogen-based power solutions. GeoPura designs, manufactures, operates, leases and sells its Hydrogen Power Units (“HPUs”), which use the Company’s fuel cell modules to convert hydrogen into electricity and provide clean, low-noise, off-grid power. GeoPura also produces green hydrogen, generated via electrolysis, at its dedicated production sites, including through its 50% ownership interest in UK-based HyMarnham Power, and holds a contract under the UK government’s inaugural Hydrogen Allocation Round 1 (HAR1), a subsidy mechanism guaranteeing hydrogen production revenues over fifteen years.

 

2.2 Acquisition Date

 

August 28, 2026.

 

2.3 Consideration

 

Consideration for the Acquisition consisted of (i) upfront consideration of £269.6 million (the “Upfront Consideration”), being the headline purchase price of £275.0 million as adjusted in accordance with the terms of the Purchase Agreement, and (ii) contingent consideration of up to £27.5 million (the “Contingent Consideration”) payable in cash and/or shares pursuant to the terms of the Purchase Agreement if GeoPura achieves certain specified financial milestones following the closing of the Acquisition (“Closing”). Any Contingent Consideration that becomes payable may be satisfied, at the Company’s sole discretion, in

 

 

 

cash, through the issuance of common shares of the Company at a price per share equal to the 30-day trailing volume-weighted average price of the common shares on the business day immediately preceding the applicable payment date, or a combination thereof. Any cash portion of the Contingent Consideration is expected to be funded from the Company’s cash on hand.

 

The Upfront Consideration was satisfied on Closing through a combination of: (a) a cash payment of £77.1 million (the “Closing Payment”), funded from the Company’s cash on hand; (b) the issuance of 49,584,212 common shares of the Company (the “Consideration Shares”) to the Sellers at a deemed price of US$5.02 per share, based on the Company’s 30-day volume-weighted average share price prior to the date of the Purchase Agreement (the “30-Day VWAP”); and (c) the grant of 1,084,540 rollover restricted share units (the “Rollover RSUs”) under the Company’s GeoPura Restricted Share Unit Plan (and not under the Company’s existing Consolidated Share Distribution Plan) in consideration for the release and cancellation of certain GeoPura options held by GeoPura optionholders. The Rollover RSUs represent 1,084,540 common shares of the Company reserved for issuance, having a deemed issue price of US$5.02 per share based on the 30-Day VWAP, and are expected to vest twelve months following Closing. The Consideration Shares and the common shares underlying the Rollover RSUs represented approximately 14.1% of the Company’s outstanding common shares on a pro forma basis. For accounting purposes, the Consideration Shares and the Rollover RSUs are measured at their estimated fair value as of Closing, based on the closing price of the common shares on the date of Closing, and the total preliminary purchase consideration, including the estimated fair value of the Contingent Consideration, is approximately US$230.7 million, as described in the unaudited pro forma condensed consolidated financial statements attached as Appendix C.

 

2.4 Effect on Financial Position

 

The effect of the Acquisition on the Company’s financial position is presented in the unaudited pro forma condensed consolidated financial statements of the Company attached as Appendix C to this business acquisition report.

 

Concurrent with Closing, the Company appointed Andrew Cunningham as its President, reporting to Marty Neese, the Company’s Chief Executive Officer, and Andrew Cunningham and Lord Richard Harrington joined the Company’s board of directors as nominees designated by the former GeoPura shareholders.

 

Except as otherwise publicly disclosed and other than in the ordinary course of integrating GeoPura into the Company’s business, the Company does not currently have any plans or proposals for material changes in the business affairs of the Company or GeoPura, including any proposal to liquidate the business, sell, lease or exchange all or a substantial part of its assets, amalgamate it with any other business organization, or make any material changes to its business, such as changes in corporate structure, management or personnel, that may have a significant effect on the financial performance and financial position of the Company.

 

The unaudited pro forma adjustments are based on preliminary estimates and assumptions made by management solely for the purpose of preparing the unaudited pro forma condensed consolidated financial statements. Changes are expected as valuations of the assets acquired and liabilities assumed are completed and as additional information becomes available, and the final purchase price allocation may differ, possibly materially, from that reflected in the unaudited pro forma condensed consolidated financial statements.

2.5 Prior Valuations

 

To the knowledge of the Company, no valuation opinion was obtained within the last 12 months by the Company or GeoPura that was required by securities legislation or a Canadian exchange or market to support the consideration paid by the Company in connection with the Acquisition.

 

2.6 Parties to Transaction

 

The Company acquired GeoPura from the Sellers. The Acquisition was not with an informed person, associate or affiliate of the Company, as such terms are defined in National Instrument 51-102 – Continuous Disclosure Obligations (“NI 51-102”) and applicable securities laws.

 

2.7 Date of Report

 

November 9, 2026.

Independent Auditor’s Report to the Members of GeoPura Ltd

 

To the Board of Directors of GeoPura Ltd.

 

Opinion

 

We have audited the consolidated financial statements of GeoPura Ltd (‘the group’), which comprise the consolidated statement of financial position as at 31 March 2026 and the consolidated statements of loss and comprehensive loss, the consolidated statements of changes in equity/(deficit), the consolidated statements of cash flows for the year then ended and the related notes, including a summary of significant accounting policies. The financial reporting framework that has been applied in their preparation is applicable law and International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRSs) as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board.

 

In our opinion the accompanying financial statements present fairly, in all material respects the consolidated financial position of the group as at March 31, 2026 and its consolidated financial performance and its consolidated cash flow for the year then ended in accordance with IFRSs as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board.

 

Basis for opinion

 

We conducted our audit in accordance with International Standards on Auditing (‘ISAs’) and applicable law. Our responsibilities under those standards are further described in the ‘Auditor’s responsibilities for the audit of the financial statements’ section of our report. We are independent of the group in accordance with the ethical requirements that are relevant to our audit of the financial statements in the United Kingdom, including the Financial Reporting Council’s Ethical Standard and we have fulfilled our other ethical responsibilities in accordance with these requirements. We believe that the audit evidence we have obtained is sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis for our opinion.

 

Responsibilities of directors

 

The directors are responsible for the preparation and fair presentation of the financial statements in accordance with IFRSs as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board, and for such internal control as the directors determine is necessary to enable the preparation of financial statements that are free from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error.

 

In preparing the financial statements, the directors are responsible for assessing the group’s ability to continue as a going concern, disclosing, as applicable, matters related to going concern and using the going concern basis of accounting unless the directors either intend to liquidate the group or to cease operations, or have no realistic alternative but to do so.

 

The directors are responsible for overseeing the Group’s financial reporting process.

 

Auditor’s responsibilities for the audit of the financial statements

 

Our objectives are to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements as a whole are free from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error, and to issue an auditor’s report that includes our opinion.

 

Reasonable assurance is a high level of assurance, but is not a guarantee that an audit conducted in accordance with ISAs will always detect a material misstatement when it exists.

 

Misstatements can arise from fraud or error and are considered material if, individually or in the aggregate, they could reasonably be expected to influence the economic decisions of users taken on the basis of these financial statements.

 

Extent to which the audit was considered capable of detecting irregularities, including fraud

 

Irregularities, including fraud, are instances of non-compliance with laws and regulations. We design procedures in line with our responsibilities, outlined above, to detect material misstatements in respect of irregularities, including fraud. The extent to which our procedures are capable of detecting irregularities, including fraud is detailed below. However, it is the primary responsibility of management, with the oversight of those charged with governance, to ensure that the entity’s operations are conducted in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and for the prevention and detection of fraud.

Independent Auditor’s Report to the Members of GeoPura Ltd (continued)

 

We obtain and update our understanding of the group, its activities, its control environment, and likely future developments, including in relation to the legal and regulatory framework applicable and how the group is complying with that framework. Based on this understanding, we identify and assess the risks of material misstatement of the financial statements, whether due to fraud or error, design and perform audit procedures responsive to those risks, and obtain audit evidence that is sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis for our opinion. This includes consideration of the risk of acts by the entity that were contrary to applicable laws and regulations, including fraud.

 

Based on our understanding of the group, we identified that the principal risks of non-compliance with laws and regulations related to laws and regulations that directly affect the financial statements including financial reporting legislation (including related companies legislation), distributable profits legislation, pension legislation and UK tax legislation. In addition, the group is subject to many other laws and regulations where the consequences of non-compliance could have a material effect on amounts or disclosures in the financial statements, for instance through the imposition of fines and litigation. We considered the extent to which non-compliance with laws and regulations might have a material effect on the financial statements and we have assessed the extent of compliance with these laws and regulations as part of our procedures on the related financial statement items.

 

We also evaluated managements’ incentives and opportunities for fraudulent manipulation of the financial statements (including the risk of override of controls) and determined that the principal risks related to posting inappropriate journal entries to manipulate financial results, management bias in accounting estimates, as well as improper revenue recognition which includes fraudulent posting of journal entries to revenue.

 

Audit procedures performed by the engagement team included:

 

·Inquiry of management and those charged with governance regarding actual and potential litigation or claims as well as whether they have knowledge of any actual, suspected or alleged fraud;

 

·Reviewing the financial statement disclosures and testing to supporting documentation to assess compliance with applicable laws and regulations;

 

·Reviewing meeting minutes to identify reported frauds and any potential non-compliance with laws and regulations;

 

·Identifying journal entries based on risk criteria and testing the identified entries to supporting documentation, in particular journal entries with unusual account combinations; and

 

·Challenging assumptions and judgments made by management in their significant accounting estimates and evaluating whether there was any evidence of bias by the directors that represented a risk of material misstatement due to fraud.

 

Because of the inherent limitations of an audit, there is a risk that we will not detect all irregularities, including those leading to a material misstatement in the financial statements or non-compliance with regulation. This risk increases the more that compliance with a law or regulation is removed from the events and transactions reflected in the financial statements, as we will be less likely to become aware of instances of non-compliance. The risk is also greater regarding irregularities occurring due to fraud rather than error, as fraud involves intentional concealment, forgery, collusion, omission or misrepresentation.

1.General information

 

GeoPura Ltd is a company limited by shares incorporated in England and Wales. The registered office is c/o Hobsons, Alexandra Street, Nottingham, NG5 1AY. The company’s registered number is 11855286. The principal activities are to deliver hydrogen-fuelled clean and sustainable energy to replace diesel generators and decarbonise customers in off-grid and grid augmentation situations. The company achieves this through an ‘energy as a service’ business model: leasing its HPUs (Hydrogen Power Units) to customers with a GeoPura engineer backed service delivery and full fuel management system to provide regular hydrogen supply. The company has one wholly-owned subsidiary, GeoPura (Europe) ApS, incorporated in Denmark on 31 July 2025; these consolidated financial statements present the results and financial position of the company and its subsidiary (together, the group).

 

The financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2026 were authorised for issue under a resolution of the directors on 9 November 2026.

 

2.Basis of preparation and statement of compliance

 

The consolidated financial statements of GeoPura Ltd (the company) and its subsidiary (together, the group) have been prepared in accordance with IFRSs as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board (IASB) and comply with those standards.

 

These are the group’s first consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with IFRS Accounting Standards as issued by the IASB, and IFRS 1 First-time Adoption of International Financial Reporting Standards has been applied. The company previously reported under FRS 102 The Financial Reporting Standard applicable in the UK and Republic of Ireland, most recently for the year ended 31 March 2025. The date of transition is 1 April 2024. The comparative information for the year ended 31 March 2025 and the opening statement of financial position at 1 April 2024 have been restated on the IFRS basis. Note 35 explains how the transition affected the reported financial position, financial performance and cash flows.

 

Basis of consolidation

 

The consolidated financial statements incorporate the financial statements of the company and its wholly-owned subsidiary, GeoPura (Europe) ApS, incorporated in Denmark. Subsidiaries are consolidated from the date on which control is obtained, and intra-group balances, transactions and unrealised gains and losses are eliminated in full. GeoPura (Europe) ApS was incorporated during the year ended 31 March 2026 and has been consolidated from incorporation; the comparative information and the opening IFRS statement of financial position at 1 April 2024 are therefore those of the company alone and are unaffected by consolidation.

 

The financial statements have been prepared on the historical cost basis, except for financial instruments measured at fair value through profit or loss (IFRS 9) and share-based payment arrangements measured at grant-date fair value (IFRS 2). The financial statements are presented in pounds sterling (£), which is the functional and presentation currency of the company. The subsidiary’s functional currency is the Danish krone; its results and financial position are translated into sterling for consolidation. Unless otherwise stated, amounts are rounded to the nearest thousand pounds (£’000), and totals may not cast exactly due to rounding.

 

The company presents assets and liabilities based on current and non-current classification. A liability is classified as current when it is due to be settled within twelve months of the reporting date or there is no right to defer settlement for at least twelve months; on this basis the convertible loan notes, which mature on 12 August 2026, are presented as current liabilities at 31 March 2026.

Going concern

 

The company has been a wholly-owned subsidiary of Ballard Power Systems Inc. since 28 August 2026. Forecasts for at least twelve months from approval show that capital expenditure and working capital depend on parent funding; Ballard has confirmed it will provide the support needed to meet liabilities as they fall due. The financial statements are therefore prepared on the going concern basis.

 

During the year the company drew asset-backed and secured debt including facilities with Barclays and HSBC (bank borrowings at 31 March 2026: £31.5 million) and increased its convertible loan notes by £27 million across the May and July 2025 tranches from existing investors including Barclays Sustainable Impact Capital, General Motors Ventures, SWEN Capital Partners, Siemens Energy Ventures and the National Wealth Fund.

 

A key consideration in the directors’ assessment is the convertible loan notes, the principal and accrued interest on which (£98.7 million contractually at 31 March 2026; carrying amount £113.2 million including the separated embedded derivative) (see note 33).

 

On the basis of this assessment the directors continue to adopt the going concern basis in preparing these financial statements.

 

3.New and forthcoming accounting standards

 

As first-time adoption of IFRS, all standards effective for periods beginning on or after 1 April 2025 have been applied from the date of transition, including the amendments to IAS 1 (Classification of Liabilities as Current or Non-current; Non-current Liabilities with Covenants), the amendments to IFRS 16 (Lease Liability in a Sale and Leaseback) and the amendments to IAS 21 (Lack of Exchangeability). These are reflected in the accounting policies rather than disclosed as changes in accounting policy.

 

Standards issued but not yet effective which may be relevant to the company are: IFRS 18 Presentation and Disclosure in Financial Statements (effective 1 January 2027), which replaces IAS 1 and introduces defined subtotals and disclosure of management-defined performance measures, the company is assessing its impact; and IFRS 19 Subsidiaries without Public Accountability: Disclosures (effective 1 January 2027), which the company’s Danish subsidiary may be eligible to apply in its own reporting. The company does not plan to adopt these standards early.

 

4.Material accounting policies

 

The company’s material accounting policies are set out below. These policies have been applied consistently to all periods presented and in preparing the opening IFRS statement of financial position at 1 April 2024, except as explained in note 35.

 

Revenue from contracts with customers

 

Revenue represents the consideration to which the company expects to be entitled in exchange for transferring goods and services to customers, excluding value added tax, recognised by applying the five-step model in IFRS 15. The company has three principal revenue streams:

 

Energy as a Service. The company supplies clean energy to customers through the hire of hydrogen power units (HPUs) together with engineer-backed service delivery and a fuel management system providing hydrogen supply.

 

Management has assessed whether these arrangements contain a lease under IFRS 16 and concluded that they do not: although the customer obtains the energy output, it is the company, rather than the customer, that directs the use of the HPUs, through its engineer-backed operation and fuel management, and the company retains substantive rights to substitute units.

 

Each arrangement is accounted for within IFRS 15: HPU rental and service is a single performance obligation satisfied over time; hydrogen supply is a distinct performance obligation for metered output, with variable consideration trued up to actual consumption; and separately priced maintenance and delivery or haulage services are distinct performance obligations recognised as the services are provided.

4.Material accounting policies (continued)

 

Project sales. Revenue from the sale of hydrogen power units and hydrogen production equipment is recognised over time where the criteria in IFRS 15 are met, in particular where the company’s performance does not create an asset with an alternative use and the company has an enforceable right to payment for performance completed to date, including through contractual termination-for-convenience compensation providing cost plus a reasonable margin, using an input method to measure progress.

 

Where those criteria are not met, revenue is recognised at the point in time when control of the equipment transfers to the customer, assessed with reference to title, physical possession, acceptance, and the transfer of significant risks and rewards.

 

Joint venture revenue

 

Revenue from services provided to the HyMarnham Power joint venture is recognised as the services are performed. Revenue relating to the supply of a production facility is recognised at a point in time when control of the facility transfers to the joint venture.

 

Variable consideration is included in the transaction price only to the extent that it is highly probable that a significant reversal will not occur. Amounts invoiced in advance of performance are recognised as contract liabilities; amounts where performance precedes invoicing are recognised as contract assets.

 

Government grants and other income

 

Government grants, including funding associated with the Hydrogen Allocation Round, are recognised when there is reasonable assurance that the company will comply with the conditions attaching to them and that the grants will be received.

 

Leases

 

At inception of a contract the company assesses whether the contract is, or contains, a lease. For each lease the company recognises a right-of-use asset and a lease liability, except for short-term leases and leases of low-value assets, for which the lease payments are recognised as an expense on a straight-line basis.

 

The lease liability is initially measured at the present value of the unpaid lease payments, discounted using the rate implicit in the lease or, if that rate cannot be readily determined, the company’s incremental borrowing rate; the right-of-use asset is initially measured at cost and depreciated over the shorter of the lease term and the useful life of the asset, except where ownership transfers at the end of the term (including hire purchase contracts), in which case the asset is depreciated over its useful life.

 

Sale and leaseback

 

Where the company sells plant and leases it back under asset-backed financing arrangements, the company first assesses whether the transfer is a sale under IFRS 15. Where control of the plant does not pass to the financier, as is the case for the company’s finance-and-buy-back arrangements, the transfer is not a sale: the plant continues to be recognised at its previous carrying amount and a financial liability equal to the proceeds is recognised within borrowings and measured at amortised cost.

 

Property, plant and equipment

 

Property, plant and equipment is stated at cost less accumulated depreciation and accumulated impairment losses. Depreciation is provided to write off the cost less estimated residual value over the estimated useful life of each asset:

 

·leasehold property improvements, HPUs, and hydrogen production equipment 10% straight line;

 

·other plant and machinery 20% straight line;

 

·motor vehicles, fixtures and fittings and computer equipment 25% reducing balance.

 

Residual values and useful lives are reviewed at each reporting date.

 

10

GeoPura Ltd

GeoPura Ltd.

 

Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (continued)

 

4.Material accounting policies (continued)

 

Intangible assets and development costs

 

Development expenditure is capitalised as an intangible asset only when the IAS 38 criteria are demonstrated. Capitalised development expenditure is stated at cost less accumulated amortisation and impairment; amortisation is charged on a straight-line basis over ten years from the date the asset is available for use and is included within administrative expenses.

 

Borrowing costs directly attributable to qualifying assets are capitalised from the commencement of development where capitalisation commenced on or after 1 April 2024 (see note 35).

 

Impairment of non-financial assets

 

At each reporting date the company reviews the carrying amounts of its non-financial assets for indications of impairment; if any exist, the recoverable amount is estimated as the higher of fair value less costs of disposal and value in use. Capitalised development expenditure not yet available for use is tested annually.

 

Inventories

 

Inventories are stated at the lower of cost and net realisable value. Cost comprises the costs of purchase and, for units manufactured or assembled by the group, the direct costs of bringing each unit to its present location and condition. Net realisable value is the estimated selling price in the ordinary course of business less the estimated costs of completion and the estimated costs necessary to make the sale.

 

Financial instruments

 

Financial assets and liabilities are recognised when the group becomes party to the contractual provisions of the instrument.

 

(i)Classification

 

Financial assets are classified as measured at amortised cost or at fair value through profit or loss (FVTPL). The classification depends on the business model for managing the assets and on their contractual cash flows. Financial liabilities are measured at amortised cost, except derivatives, which are measured at FVTPL. The group holds no instruments at fair value through other comprehensive income.

 

  Classification under IFRS 9
Cash and cash equivalents Amortised cost
Trade and other receivables Amortised cost
Trade and other payables Amortised cost
Borrowings, including asset-backed finance Amortised cost
Convertible loan notes: host debt Amortised cost
Convertible loan notes: embedded derivative FVTPL

 

Lease liabilities are measured under IFRS 16.

 

11

GeoPura Ltd

GeoPura Ltd.

 

Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (continued)

 

4.Material accounting policies (continued)

 

(ii)Measurement

 

Amortised cost: Financial assets and liabilities at amortised cost are first measured at fair value. Directly attributable transaction costs are added for assets and deducted for liabilities. Trade receivables without a significant financing component are first measured at the transaction price. After that, these instruments are measured at amortised cost using the effective interest method. Financial assets are shown net of the loss allowance.

 

FVTPL: Instruments at FVTPL are first measured at fair value, and transaction costs are expensed. They are remeasured at fair value at each reporting date, and gains and losses go to profit or loss.

 

Convertible loan notes: The conversion feature does not meet the fixed-for-fixed condition in IAS 32. The conversion price varies with the pricing of a future funding round, subject to a cap, and the class of shares delivered varies with the conversion event. The notes are therefore a financial liability in full. The conversion triggers, the exit payoff and the noteholder put are separated from the host as a single compound embedded derivative. At issue, the embedded derivative is measured at fair value. The host is measured as the residual of the proceeds, net of transaction costs. The host is then measured at amortised cost using the effective interest method. The embedded derivative is remeasured at fair value at each reporting date using a probability-weighted scenario model (note 30), and changes go to profit or loss. The host and the embedded derivative are presented together within convertible loan notes.

 

(iii)Impairment of financial assets and contract assets

 

The group recognises a loss allowance for ECL on financial assets at amortised cost and on contract assets. For trade receivables and contract assets, it applies the simplified approach and measures the allowance at lifetime ECL. For other financial assets, the allowance is 12-month ECL. If credit risk has increased significantly since initial recognition, lifetime ECL is used instead. Movements in the allowance go to profit or loss.

 

(iv)Derecognition

 

Financial assets: A financial asset is derecognised when the rights to its cash flows expire. It is also derecognised when the asset is transferred together with substantially all the risks and rewards of ownership.

 

Financial liabilities: A financial liability is derecognised when the obligation is discharged, cancelled or expires. If the terms are modified substantially, the original liability is derecognised and a new liability is recognised at fair value. The difference between the carrying amount derecognised and the consideration paid goes to profit or loss.

4.Material accounting policies (continued)

 

Foreign currency

 

The functional and presentation currency of the company is pounds sterling. Transactions in foreign currencies, including the company’s euro-denominated lease and its Danish krone balances, are translated at the spot rate at the date of the transaction; monetary assets and liabilities denominated in foreign currencies are translated at the closing rate, with exchange differences recognised in profit or loss.

 

Taxation

 

The tax expense comprises current and deferred tax. Research and development tax reliefs and credits are recognised when it is probable that they will be received. Deferred tax is recognised on temporary differences between the carrying amounts of assets and liabilities and their tax bases; deferred tax assets are recognised only to the extent that it is probable that future taxable profits will be available.

 

Share-based payments

 

The company operates an equity-settled Company Share Option Plan (CSOP) for employees. The grant-date fair value of awards is recognised as an employee expense over the vesting period, with a corresponding increase in equity, adjusted for the number of awards expected to vest under non-market vesting conditions. Where vesting accelerates, for example on a change of control under the scheme rules, the remaining unrecognised charge is recognised at the acceleration date.

 

Employee benefits, provisions, cash and share capital

 

Short-term employee benefits are recognised as an expense as the service is received; the company operates a defined contribution pension scheme.

 

Provisions

 

Provisions are recognised for present obligations arising from past events where an outflow is probable and can be reliably estimated.

 

Cash and cash equivalents

 

Cash and cash equivalents comprise cash at bank and in hand and short-term deposits of three months or less.

 

Reserves

 

Ordinary shares and Series A shares are classified as equity, with incremental issue costs recognised as a deduction from equity.

5.Critical accounting judgements and key sources of estimation uncertainty

 

Significant judgements

 

Classification of the convertible loan notes. The directors have assessed, under IAS 32, that the conversion feature does not meet the fixed-for-fixed condition, because the conversion price varies with future funding-round pricing and the class of shares varies with the conversion event; the notes are therefore a financial liability in full with a separated compound embedded derivative.

 

Sale and leaseback. The directors have concluded that the asset-backed financing transactions entered into during the years ended 31 March 2025 and 31 March 2026 do not transfer control of the plant and are accounted for as secured borrowings.

 

Capitalisation of development expenditure. The directors assess whether development projects, including the HPU 2, meet the IAS 38 capitalisation criteria.

 

Key sources of estimation uncertainty

 

Fair value of the embedded derivative within the convertible loan notes: measured using a probability-weighted scenario model with unobservable inputs, including the probabilities of pre-maturity conversion, maturity conversion and exit events, calibrated to third-party market interest rate quotes at issue.

 

Fair value of share-based payment awards: the grant-date fair value of the CSOP options is measured using a Black-Scholes model, with the share value at each grant date taken from contemporaneous funding-round pricing (£50.54-£185.00 per share) and expected volatility of 50-52%.

Bank and other loans

 

Bank and other loans comprise facilities with Barclays (£28.1 million) and HSBC (£3.4 million, including an asset loan of £4.7 million original principal repayable in monthly instalments to September 2029 secured over plant), together with a Bounce Back Loan. The obligations arising on the asset-backed financing transactions described below are presented within borrowings as secured borrowings (2026: £14.7 million; 2025: £10.7 million); the H2 Production Doncaster facility is presented within lease liabilities (note 24). The current portions of the bank loans are the instalments contractually due within twelve months: at 31 March 2026, £5.1 million on the Barclays facility (£27 million drawn November 2025, semi-annual repayments from September 2026, maturing March 2032) and £0.9m on the HSBC asset loan, together with the residual Bounce Back Loan; at 31 March 2025, £1.1 million on the HSBC asset loan and the Bounce Back Loan instalment. The Eurotainer sale-and-hire-back is repayable by monthly instalments of EUR 40.950k to December 2040 (undiscounted £6.3 million at the transaction rate), secured on the 10 MEGC trailers concerned.

 

Asset-backed financing arrangements

 

During the year ended 31 March 2025 the company entered into four sale-and-hire-purchase-back transactions, with Siemens Financial Services, Close Brothers (two arrangements) and BNP Paribas, for proceeds of £11,996k. During the year ended 31 March 2026 it entered into two further arrangements, with Siemens Financial Services and Close Brothers, for proceeds of £8,692k. In December 2025 the company also transferred 10 MEGC trailers to Eurotainer for EUR 3.4 million and hired them back for 15 years; title and control were retained, so the proceeds are a secured borrowing within long-term debt and the trailers remain in property, plant and equipment. Control of the plant did not pass to the financiers and none of the transfers is a sale under IFRS 15: the plant continues to be recognised within property, plant and equipment and the proceeds are recognised as secured borrowings measured at amortised cost.

 

Convertible loan notes

 

The convertible loan notes comprise three tranches: £56 million issued in February 2024 at 14%, £16 million issued in May 2025 at 16% and £11 million issued in July 2025 at 18% - £83 million principal in aggregate. Interest accrues and rolls up from issue; unless converted, the principal and accrued interest are due on 12 August 2026, and the notes are accordingly presented as current liabilities at 31 March 2026. The contractual balance at 31 March 2026 of £98.7 million comprises the £83 million principal and accrued interest, less unamortised arrangement fees. The carrying amount comprises the host liability at amortised cost of £101.5 million (2025: £61.2 million) and the embedded derivative at fair value of £11.7 million (2025: £1.4 million) - see notes 30 and 35. The notes are classified as current at 31 March 2026, as the 12 August 2026 maturity falls within twelve months of the reporting date; at 31 March 2025 and 1 April 2024 they are classified as non-current, consistent with their contractual maturity at those dates.

28.Share-based payments

 

The company operates an equity-settled Company Share Option Plan (CSOP). Options were granted under the CSOP over £1.00 ordinary shares at an exercise price of £24.45 per share on 20 October 2023 (41,573 options), 27 November 2023 (3,172 options), 22 July 2024 (14,807 options), 3 February 2026 (6,903 options) and 2 June 2026 (33,933 options). Options vest three years from the vesting-commencement date, subject to continued employment, and have a ten-year contractual life; in practice exercise is expected on an exit event. Under the scheme rules, options become exercisable in full, vested and unvested, on a change of control of the company.

 

The awards were unvested at the date of transition, so the IFRS 1 D2 exemption is not available and IFRS 2 is applied in full: the grant-date fair value, measured using a Black-Scholes model, is recognised over each three-year vesting period, with a cumulative catch-up in opening retained earnings at 1 April 2024 and charges in each of FY25 and FY26. For the June 2026 awards, employees began rendering services from the vesting-commencement date of 25 February 2026, before the legal grant date; the charge is therefore recognised from that date based on an estimate of the grant-date fair value. The February 2026 awards are recognised from their grant date, which is also their vesting-commencement date. Both awards are included in the movements below. The announced acquisition of the company (note 33) would accelerate the residual unvested charge into FY27.

29.Financial instruments, risk management

 

Credit risk

 

The company applies the IFRS 9 simplified approach, measuring lifetime expected credit losses on trade receivables and contract assets. Expected credit losses are not material at any date presented; the principal other receivables are capital equipment deposits and the euro reserve account, which the directors assess for recoverability by reference to the counterparties and the underlying projects.

 

Liquidity risk

 

The company’s most significant liquidity exposure is the maturity of the convertible loan notes on 12 August 2026 (£113.2 million carrying amount at 31 March 2026 (contractual principal and interest at maturity: £107.6 million)), addressed through the expected conversion on completion of the announced acquisition (note 33) and the going concern assessment in note 2. The following table shows the contractual undiscounted cash flows of financial liabilities at 31 March 2026:

 

  Within 1 yr 1-2 yrs 2-5 yrs    Over 5 yrs Total
Convertible loan notes 107,648 - - - 107,648
Bank borrowings and asset-backed financing obligations 14,634 13,495 26,213 5,448 59,790
Lease liabilities 656 488 981 697 2,822
Trade payables and accruals (financial liabilities) 5,833 - - - 5,833
Total 128,771 13,983 27,194 6,145 176,093

 

The convertible loan note amount within one year is the £83m principal plus rolled-up interest to the 12 August 2026 maturity (£107.6m in aggregate).

 

Market risk

 

The company is exposed to interest rate risk on floating-rate borrowings, and to foreign currency risk principally on its euro-denominated lease and contract balances and its Danish krone balances with the subsidiary. The fair value of the embedded derivative within the convertible loan notes is exposed to changes in the probability and pricing of the conversion scenarios. The estimated effect on the loss before tax of reasonably possible changes in each risk variable, with all other variables held constant, is:

Capital management

 

The company manages its capital to ensure it can continue as a going concern while funding the growth of the HPU fleet, monitoring net debt (borrowings and lease liabilities less cash) against equity. The capital structure at 31 March 2026 comprised net debt of £156.8 million and net liabilities of £46.3 million, reflecting the classification of the convertible loan notes as debt pending their expected conversion.

30.Fair value measurement

 

The disclosure of the fair value of financial instruments is based on the following fair value hierarchy:

 

·Level 1: Quoted, unadjusted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities.

 

·Level 2: Inputs other than quoted prices included within Level 1 that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly.

 

·Level 3: Unobservable inputs for the asset or liability.

 

The compound embedded derivative separated from the convertible loan notes is measured at fair value through profit or loss and is categorised within Level 3 of the fair value hierarchy. It is valued using a probability-weighted scenario model whose significant unobservable inputs are the probabilities of pre-maturity conversion, conversion at maturity and exit settlement, with issue-date values calibrated to third-party bank quotes for equivalent non-convertible debt.

The fair value is most sensitive to the expected equity value per share: a decrease from £185.00 to £180.00 would decrease the year-end fair value by £2.3 million, and reversion to the £163.03 contractual maturity conversion price would decrease it by £10.0 million. A 5 percentage point increase in the probability of pre-maturity conversion would increase the fair value by £1.1 million. The valuation is calibrated to quotations obtained from third-party lenders for equivalent non-convertible debt (market yields of 15.5%, 18.1%).

32.Related party transactions

 

The company’s related parties comprise its directors and other key management personnel, its shareholders, its subsidiary GeoPura (Europe) ApS and the HyMarnham Power joint venture. Unless otherwise stated, transactions with related parties were carried out on an arm’s length basis.

 

Shareholders

 

The convertible loan notes were issued to shareholders including Barclays Sustainable Impact Capital, General Motors Ventures, SWEN Capital Partners, Siemens Energy Ventures and the National Wealth Fund; £27 million of notes were issued during the year (May and July 2025 tranches) and interest of £13.9 million (2025: £8.7 million) accrued during the year on the effective interest basis, with the notes and accrued interest outstanding at the year end (note 23).

 

During the year, the company made sales of £nil (2025: £nil) to, and purchases of £11,477k (£11,737k) from certain shareholders of the company. At the year end, the company was owed £nil (2025: £nil) from, and owed £599k (2025: £1,805k) to, certain shareholders of the company.

 

Subsidiary

 

Balances and transactions between the company and its subsidiary, including the intercompany loan to GeoPura (Europe) ApS, are eliminated on consolidation and are not disclosed here; they will be disclosed in the parent company’s individual financial statements.

 

Joint venture

 

At 31 March 2026 the group held £27.2 million of units and work in progress for transfer to the HyMarnham Power joint venture, presented within inventories (note 17); these were sold to the joint venture after the year end (note 33).

 

Directors

 

During the year, the company reimbursed expenses of £2k (2025: £28k) to certain directors of the company.

 

33.Events after the reporting period

 

Acquisition by Ballard Power Systems Inc. The sale agreed on 23 June 2026 (£275 million upfront, up to £27.5 million contingent) completed on 28 August 2026. All 100,388 options were exercised at £24.45 and the shares sold to Ballard; 25,090 ESOP options were replaced by Ballard restricted share units. The unrecognised fair value of the vested options is charged to completion. Transaction costs and completion bonuses of c.£4.8m were incurred.

 

Convertible loan notes. A deed after the year end set the maturity conversion price at £150. On 12 August 2026 the notes converted into 717,621 shares; the host liability and the derivative (remeasured to £27.4m) were derecognised and £135.0 million credited to equity.

 

High Marnham joint venture. In April 2026 the company completed the EPC supply, transferred the £27.2 million of production units held in inventories (note 17) and recognised revenue of £27.4 million, settled by the £2.0 million subscription and £27.0 million of loans to the venture, which is equity accounted from that date.

 

Share options: 33,933 options were granted on 2 June 2026 (fair value £160.90), recognised from the 25 February 2026 vesting-commencement date; after the sale agreement the expected vesting date became the completion date.

35.Explanation of transition to IFRS

 

These are the group’s first consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with IFRS Accounting Standards as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board (IASB), and IFRS 1 First-time Adoption of International Financial Reporting Standards has been applied. For periods up to and including the year ended 31 March 2025, the company prepared its financial statements in accordance with FRS 102 (previous GAAP). The date of transition is 1 April 2024. In preparing its opening IFRS statement of financial position and comparative information, the company has adjusted amounts reported previously under FRS 102. This note explains the principal adjustments and their effect on the company’s financial position, financial performance and cash flows.

 

Optional exemptions applied

 

Lease definition (IFRS 1.D9). The company has assessed whether contracts existing at the date of transition contain a lease on the basis of facts and circumstances at that date.

 

Leases (IFRS 1.D9B and D9D). Lease liabilities for leases previously classified as operating leases have been measured at the present value of the remaining lease payments at 1 April 2024, discounted using the incremental borrowing rate at that date, with right-of-use assets measured at an amount equal to the lease liability, adjusted for prepaid or accrued lease payments. The D9D practical expedients, including a single discount rate for portfolios of similar leases and the exclusion of leases ending within twelve months of transition, have been applied where relevant.

 

Deemed cost (IFRS 1.D5-D8). Not applied: previous GAAP measured property, plant and equipment under the cost model, so full retrospective application of IAS 16 produces the same carrying amounts.

 

Borrowing costs (IFRS 1.D23). IAS 23 is applied to borrowing costs relating to qualifying assets for which the commencement date for capitalisation is on or after 1 April 2024.

 

Share-based payments (IFRS 1.D2). The exemption is available only for awards that vested before the date of transition. The company’s CSOP options were unvested at 1 April 2024, so the exemption does not apply and IFRS 2 has been applied to those awards in full.

 

30

GeoPura Ltd

Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (continued)

 

35.Explanation of transition to IFRS (continued)

 

Mandatory exceptions applied

 

Estimates at 1 April 2024 and 31 March 2025 are consistent with those made at the same dates under FRS 102, adjusted only for differences in accounting policies (IFRS 1.14-17). Classification and measurement of financial assets is assessed on the facts at the date of transition (IFRS 1.B8-B8C). The expected credit loss requirements are applied using reasonable and supportable information available at transition without undue cost or effort (IFRS 1.B8D). Whether an embedded derivative is separated from its host contract is assessed on the conditions at the later of the date the company first became a party to the contract and the date a reassessment is required by IFRS 9 (IFRS 1.B9). Derecognition of financial assets and liabilities is applied prospectively from the date of transition (IFRS 1.B2-B3); hedge accounting and non-controlling interests are not applicable.

 

Adjustments arising on transition

 

(a) Convertible loan notes (IAS 32 / IFRS 9). The conversion feature fails the fixed-for-fixed condition, so the notes are a liability in full and the FRS 102 convertible loan note reserve reverses. The conversion features are a single embedded derivative at fair value through profit or loss and the host is carried at amortised cost. Equity effect £(1.7) million at 1 April 2024 and £(0.6)m at 31 March 2025; FY25 finance cost £1.1m lower.

 

(b) Share-based payments (IFRS 2). The unvested options are expensed over their vesting periods at grant-date fair value, with employer payroll taxes provided on the unapproved options. The charge is credited to contributed surplus, so the equity effect is limited to the NIC provision (£5k at 1 April 2024; £18k at 31 March 2025); FY25 loss £786k higher.

 

(c) Leases (IFRS 16). Vehicle leases are recognised as right-of-use assets and lease liabilities; hire purchase obligations other than the asset-backed financing are presented as lease liabilities. Equity effect nil at 1 April 2024 and £(12)k at 31 March 2025.

 

(d) Asset-backed financing (IFRS 16.98-103). The sale-and-hire-purchase-back arrangements do not transfer control of the plant, so the plant remains in property, plant and equipment and the proceeds (£11,996k in FY25 and £8,692k in FY26) are secured borrowings; the FRS 102 deferred loss reverses. All arrangements post-date 1 April 2024. Equity effect £0.4 million at 31 March 2025; FY25 loss £0.4m lower.

 

(e) Presentation (IFRS 15 / IAS 20). Grant income and damages are presented within finance income (loss) and other; accrued and deferred income as contract assets and liabilities; and the hydrogen production units held for the joint venture as inventories. No effect on equity or the loss.

 

(f) Expected credit losses (IFRS 9). Not material at any date presented; no adjustment.

 

(g) R&D credit (IAS 20) and deferred tax (IAS 12). The R&D credit is government assistance: for FY25, £588k is deducted from intangible assets and £196k recognised in other income, and the receivable is shown as R&D credit receivable (note 12). Equity effect £(588)k at 31 March 2025. No net deferred tax is recognised at any date: the liability on fixed asset timing differences is covered by unrecognised losses (note 18).

 

(h) Borrowing costs (IAS 23). The difference from the interest capitalised under FRS 102 is c.£0.1 million in aggregate and is not adjusted.

1.General information

 

GeoPura Ltd (the “Company”) is a private company limited by shares, incorporated in England and Wales, with its registered office in Nottingham, United Kingdom. The unaudited condensed consolidated interim financial statements comprise the Company and its subsidiary GeoPura (Europe) ApS (together, the “Group”). The Group supplies hydrogen-fuelled power as a service through its fleet of hydrogen power units, sells hydrogen power units and hydrogen production equipment, and holds a 50% interest in HyMarnham Power Ltd, a joint venture producing hydrogen at High Marnham. On June 23, 2026 the Company’s shareholders agreed to sell the Company to Ballard Power Systems Inc.; the acquisition was completed on August 28, 2026 (note 21).

 

2.Basis of preparation and statement of compliance

 

These condensed consolidated interim financial statements have been prepared in accordance with IAS 34 Interim Financial Reporting as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board. They do not include all of the information required for full annual financial statements and should be read together with the Group’s financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2026.

 

The financial statements for the interim period ended June 30, 2026 were authorised for issue under a resolution of the directors on November 9, 2026.

 

The financial statements are prepared on the historical cost basis, except for the embedded derivative within the convertible loan notes, which is measured at fair value through profit or loss, and share-based compensation, which is measured at grant-date fair value. They are presented in pounds sterling, the functional currency of the Company, rounded to the nearest thousand; the subsidiary’s functional currency is the Danish krone and exchange differences on its translation are recognised in other comprehensive income.

 

Going concern

 

The company has been a wholly-owned subsidiary of Ballard Power Systems Inc. since August 28, 2026. Forecasts for at least twelve months from approval show that capital expenditure and working capital depend on parent funding; Ballard has confirmed it will provide the support needed to meet liabilities as they fall due. The financial statements are therefore prepared on the going concern basis.

 

3.Material accounting policies

 

The accounting policies applied are those set out in the Group’s financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2026.

 

The Group’s 50% interest in HyMarnham Power Ltd, which commenced operations in April 2026, is accounted for using the equity method from that date (note 9). The investment is initially recognised at cost and subsequently adjusted to recognise the Group’s share of the joint venture’s profit or loss and other comprehensive income.

 

The Group also considers long-term interests that, in substance, form part of its net investment in the joint venture when determining the extent to which the Group’s share of losses is recognised. Once the Group’s interest in the joint venture has been reduced to nil, additional losses are recognised only to the extent that the Group has incurred legal or constructive obligations or made payments on behalf of the joint venture.

 

Loans to the joint venture that do not form part of the Group’s net investment are accounted for separately as financial assets.

 

Standards issued but not yet effective which may be relevant to the company are: IFRS 18 Presentation and Disclosure in Financial Statements (effective 1 January 2027), which replaces IAS 1 and introduces defined subtotals and disclosure of management-defined performance measures, the company is assessing its impact; and IFRS 19 Subsidiaries without Public Accountability: Disclosures (effective 1 January 2027), which the company’s Danish subsidiary may be eligible to apply in its own reporting. The company does not plan to adopt these standards early.

9.Investment in and loans to joint venture

 

HyMarnham Power Ltd is a joint venture developing a hydrogen production facility at High Marnham. In April 2026 the Group subscribed £2.0 million of equity and subordinated debt and advanced £27.0 million under loan facilities A and B, together with a £5.95 million VAT facility loan within trade and other receivables.

 

The Group accounts for its 50% interest under the equity method: its share of the joint venture’s loss before tax for the quarter (£590k) is recognised against the investment.

 

The supply of equipment to the joint venture was made at a loss, so no unrealised margin arises. To March 31, 2026 the joint venture had not commenced operations and the investment was carried at cost. Facility A (£20.0 million, Bank Rate plus 7.17%) is repayable in six-monthly instalments from September 30, 2026 to March 31, 2032 and Facility B (£7.0 million, Bank Rate plus 8.17%) from September 30, 2032 to March 31, 2035; interest is paid at the end of each six-month interest period. The instalments due within twelve months (£3.0 million) and the interest accrued to June 30, 2026 (£511k, received September 30, 2026) are presented as current.

 

Long-term purchase agreement

 

The Group has entered into a long-term hydrogen purchase agreement with HyMarnham Power Limited under which the Group has committed to purchase hydrogen produced by the joint venture over the term of the agreement. The agreement includes minimum purchase commitments and pricing mechanisms governing the amounts payable by the Group for hydrogen supplied.

 

Take-cost recovery mechanism

 

Under the hydrogen purchase arrangements with HyMarnham Power Ltd, the Group is subject to a take-cost recovery mechanism for the period from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2028. Where revenues generated by the hydrogen production facility are insufficient to cover specified operating costs and financing costs, the Group may be required to make additional payments to HyMarnham Power Ltd in accordance with the contractual mechanism. The arrangement is intended to support recovery of specified costs during the initial operating period of the facility. An accrual was made for this in the period of £0.5 million.

 

Take-or-pay commitment

 

Under the hydrogen purchase agreement with HyMarnham Power Limited, the Group is subject to minimum hydrogen purchase commitments. Where the minimum contracted quantities are not taken, the Group may nevertheless be required to make payments in accordance with the take-or-pay provisions of the agreement.

 

At 30 June 2026, the Group’s estimated minimum contractual commitment under these arrangements was £100 million, of which £nil is payable within one year and £100 million thereafter.

20.Financial instruments and fair value

 

The embedded derivative in the convertible loan notes is the only instrument measured at fair value; it is classified in Level 3 of the fair value hierarchy, valued on the scenario model described in note 13 with the equity value per share, the discount rate and the scenario weighting as unobservable inputs. The carrying amounts of financial assets and liabilities at amortised cost approximate their fair values. The term loan and the loans to the joint venture bear interest at floating rates, SONIA or Bank Rate plus a margin. The asset-backed financing and sale-and-hire-back obligations bear fixed rates, are repaid in instalments, and were entered into between August 2024 and June 2026, and there has been no significant change in market rates or the Group’s credit risk that would cause a material difference.

1.General Information and Description of the Transaction

 

On August 28, 2026, Ballard Power Systems Inc. (the “Company” or “Ballard”) completed the acquisition (the “Transaction”) of GeoPura Ltd. (“GeoPura”), a UK-based provider of zero-emission, hydrogen-based power solutions.

 

GeoPura designs, manufactures, and operates Hydrogen Power Units™, or HPUs™, that offers clean, low-noise, off-grid power. Utilizing Ballard fuel cell modules at their core, these advanced systems convert hydrogen into clean electricity. GeoPura also produces green hydrogen, generated via electrolysis, at its dedicated production facilities and transports it with the UK’s largest compressed hydrogen distribution fleet.

 

The Transaction was completed for total preliminary consideration of $230.7 million consisting of (i) cash paid on closing of $104.7 million (or £77.1 million), (ii) contingent consideration of up to $37.3 million (or £27.5 million), based on the achievement of certain project and revenue milestones through December 31, 2028, payable at Ballard’s discretion in either cash, Ballard common shares (priced at the 30-day trailing VWAP before the payment date), or a combination thereof, which was fair valued using a probability-weighted, scenario-based approach at $12.4 million (or £9.2 million) on closing, (iii) 49.584 million newly issued Ballard common shares fair valued at Ballard’s closing day share price of $2.25 per share, or $111.6 million on closing, and (iv) 1.085 million Ballard restricted common share units which will be settled 12-months post-closing fair valued based on Ballard’s closing share price of $2.25 per share discounted using an appropriate discount rate to $2.0 million on closing. On a pro-forma basis, former GeoPura shareholders hold approximately 14.1% of Ballard’s outstanding common shares.

 

2.Basis of Presentation

 

These unaudited pro forma consolidated financial statements as at and for the six months ended June 30, 2026 and for the latest fiscal year (the “Pro Forma Financial Statements”) have been prepared by management of Ballard to give effect to the Transaction for the purposes of inclusion in the Business Acquisition Report of the Company dated November 9, 2026.

 

The unaudited Pro Forma Financial Statements present the pro forma consolidated financial position and results of operations of the combined company based upon the historical financial statements of Ballard and GeoPura, after giving effect to the Transaction including the conversion and settlement of certain of GeoPura’s indebtedness on closing, payment of certain of GeoPura’s transaction costs and change of control costs in connection with the Transaction on closing, and other adjustments described in these notes, and are intended to reflect the impact of the Transaction on Ballard’s consolidated financial statements. The unaudited Pro Forma Financial Statements have been prepared in accordance with IFRS and are presented in United States dollars unless otherwise disclosed.

 

·The unaudited pro forma consolidated statement of financial position as at June 30, 2026 combines the unaudited historical consolidated statement of financial position of Ballard as of June 30, 2026 and the unaudited historical consolidated statement of financial position of GeoPura as of June 30, 2026, giving effect to the Transaction as if it had been completed on June 30, 2026.

 

·The unaudited pro forma statement of loss and other comprehensive loss for the latest fiscal year combines the audited historical consolidated statement of loss and other

comprehensive loss of Ballard for the year ended December 31, 2025 and the audited historical consolidated statement of loss of GeoPura for the year ended March 31, 2026, giving effect to the Transaction as if it had been completed on January 1, 2025, the beginning of Ballard Power’s most recently completed fiscal year.

 

·The unaudited pro forma statement of loss and other comprehensive loss for the six months ended June 30, 2026 combines the unaudited historical consolidated condensed statement of loss and other comprehensive loss of Ballard for the six months ended June 30, 2026 and the unaudited historical consolidated statement of loss of GeoPura for the three months ended June 30, 2026 and the management constructed unaudited historical consolidated statement of loss of Geopura for the three months ended March 31, 2026, giving effect to the Transaction as if it had been completed on January 1, 2025, the beginning of Ballard Power’s most recently completed fiscal year.

 

These Pro Forma Financial Statements utilize accounting policies that are consistent with those disclosed in the audited financial statements of the Company for the year ended December 31, 2025, which were prepared in accordance with recognition and measurement principles of International Financial Reporting Standards (“IFRS”) as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board (“IASB”). In preparing the Pro Forma Financial Statements, a review was undertaken to identify accounting policy differences between the accounting policies used by Ballard and those of GeoPura. The review of the material accounting policies of the Company and GeoPura was necessary to ensure comparability in the Pro Forma Financial Statements. Based on our review, we believe the material accounting policies of GeoPura conform, in all material aspects, to those of Ballard, with the exception of certain presentation and reclassification adjustments summarized below in note 3.

 

The Transaction will be accounted for using the acquisition method of accounting in accordance with IFRS 3, Business Combinations. As the accounting acquirer, Ballard will account for the transaction by using Ballard’s historical information and accounting policies and adding the assets and liabilities of GeoPura at their respective fair values as of the completion date of the Transaction being August 28, 2026. The determination of the fair value of the net assets acquired is preliminary, pending finalization of various estimates and analyses. Since these Pro Forma Financial Statements have been prepared based on preliminary estimates of purchase consideration and fair values of assets and liabilities attributable to the combination, the actual amounts eventually recorded for the Transaction may differ materially from the information presented.

 

The Pro Forma Financial Statements do not reflect the impact of possible revenue or earnings enhancements or cost savings from operating efficiencies or synergies. Also, the Pro Forma Financial Statements do not reflect possible adjustments related to restructuring or integration activities that have yet to be determined or transaction or other costs following the Transaction that are not expected to have a continuing impact on the business of the combined company.

 

The historical consolidated financial information of Ballard and GeoPura has been adjusted in the Pro Forma Financial Statements to give effect to pro forma events that are (i) directly attributable to the Transaction, (ii) factually supportable, and (iii) with respect to the pro forma statements of income (loss), expected to have a continuing impact on the combined results. The Pro Forma Financial Statements should be read in conjunction with the accompanying notes to the Pro Forma Financial Statements. 4.Preliminary Purchase Price and Fair Values of Assets Acquired and Liabilities Assumed

 

The Transaction has been accounted for using the acquisition method. The preliminary allocation of the purchase price was based on a preliminary assessment of the fair value of identifiable assets, including assets acquired and liabilities assumed at the effective date of the Transaction, with the excess of the purchase price over the estimated fair value being allocated to Goodwill.

 

The Company has engaged independent valuators to determine the fair value of the consideration paid and the fair value of acquired assets and liabilities assumed. However, given the timing of the Transaction, the independent valuators have not completed the valuation, including the valuation of intangible assets, and therefore the purchase price allocation is based on the Company’s best estimate and is considered preliminary. As a result, the purchase price allocation is preliminary and is subject to change once the final valuation of the consideration paid and the identifiable assets acquired and liabilities assumed is completed.

 

The following is a preliminary fair value estimate of the consideration paid and a preliminary fair value estimate of the identifiable assets acquired and liabilities assumed by the Company in connection with the Transaction, reconciled to the estimated purchase price.

 

The Transaction was completed for total preliminary consideration of $230.7 million consisting of (i) cash paid on closing of $104.7 million (or £77.1 million), (ii) contingent consideration of up to $37.3 million (or £27.5 million), based on the achievement of certain project and revenue milestones through December 31, 2028, payable at Ballard’s discretion in either cash, Ballard common shares (priced at the 30-day trailing VWAP before the payment date), or a combination thereof, which was fair valued using a probability-weighted, scenario-based approach at $12.4 million (or £9.2 million) on closing, (iii) 49.584 million newly issued Ballard common shares fair valued at Ballard’s closing day share price of $2.25 per share, or $111.6 million on closing, and (iv) 1.085 million Ballard restricted common share units which will be settled 12-months post-closing fair valued based on Ballard’s closing share price of $2.25 per share discounted using an appropriate discount rate to $2.0 million on closing.

5.Pro Forma and Purchase Price Adjustments:

 

The following summarizes the pro forma adjustments including the purchase price adjustments in connection with the Transaction to give effect to the Transaction as if it had occurred on January 1, 2025 for purposes of the unaudited Pro Forma Consolidated Statement of Loss and Other Comprehensive Loss for the latest fiscal year; and on June 30, 2026 for purposes of the unaudited Pro Forma Consolidated Statement of Financial Position. (b)Trade and other receivables

 

Reflects a decrease of ($2,958) to trade and other receivables to eliminate intercompany receivables between Ballard and GeoPura as at June 30, 2026.

 

(c)Property, plant and equipment

 

Reflects a net increase of $452 to property, plant and equipment consisting of estimated preliminary fair value changes on certain acquired property, plant and equipment, compared to their historic cost net of amortization. Acquired property, plant and equipment consists primarily of GeoPura’s HPU fleet and other hydrogen energy production assets, leased vehicles, and other corporate assets in support of business operations and are expected to be amortized on a straight-line basis over their estimated useful life of 10-years.

6.Overlapping Period:

 

The unaudited pro forma statement of loss and other comprehensive loss for the latest fiscal year includes GeoPura’s results for the year ended March 31, 2026, and the unaudited pro forma statement of loss and other comprehensive loss for the six months ended June 30, 2026 includes GeoPura’s results for the six months ended June 30, 2026, which were constructed by management by combining GeoPura’s unaudited results for the three months ended June 30, 2026 with GeoPura’s unaudited results for the three months ended March 31, 2026. Accordingly, GeoPura’s results for the three months ended March 31, 2026 are included in both pro forma statements of loss and other comprehensive loss. The constructed results were prepared solely for the purpose of these Pro Forma Financial Statements, have not been audited or reviewed and do not conform with the financial statements of GeoPura included in Appendices A and B to the Business Acquisition Report.

 

The pro forma statement of loss and other comprehensive loss for the latest fiscal year includes, for the overlapping period, revenue of $4,925, expenses of $19,112 (comprising cost of product and service revenues of $5,560, operating expenses of $5,784 and net finance expense of $7,768), gross margin (loss) of $(635), and loss from continuing operations of $(14,187), all translated at the average exchange rate for the year ended March 31, 2026 of £1.00 per $1.34 USD.

 

The pro forma statement of loss and other comprehensive loss for the six months ended June 30, 2026 includes, for the overlapping period, revenue of $4,942, expenses of $19,177 (comprising cost of product and service revenues of $5,579, operating expenses of $5,804 and net finance expense of $7,794), gross margin (loss) of $(637), and loss from continuing operations of $(14,234), all translated at the average exchange rate for the six months ended June 30, 2026 of £1.00 per $1.3445 USD.
